messages:
sara: Hey team — just got an escalation from AcmeCorp. Their integration started returning 503s after we rotated API keys for their org this morning. They're seeing intermittent successes but roughly ~30% of requests are failing. Not seeing errors on our side at first glance. Any idea? :eyes:

lee: Thanks for the ping. Which rotation flow did we run for them? Was it a staged rotate+revoke or rotate-with-grace?

sara: We ran the standard rotate -> update -> revoke sequence using our UI. The UI showed success for all workers. Their SDK logs show `401` turning into `503` on our gateway. Jordan from CS has forwarded a couple example request IDs.

jordan: Posted two request ids: `req_42a1` and `req_42a2`. Customer says the failures started ~09:12 UTC after the rotate completed at 09:10. They were on Dedicated capacity.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-780 — "AcmeCorp post-rotation auth errors". Paging @oncall.

amy: I can look at gateway traces. Quick hypothesis: some proxies or edge nodes still have the old key cached and are sending to internal services that expect the new key format, causing mismatch and the gateway to return 503. But 503 is odd for auth — usually 401/403. Any gateway middleware mapping errors?

ryan: I'll check sidecar secret propagation. We had one rollout to the vault-agent sidecar yesterday that changed the refresh interval from 30s -> 5m (trying to reduce load). If the sidecar caches the old credential and the revocation was immediate, that could cause a fraction of pods to keep presenting revoked creds to upstream and trigger fallback behavior.

lee: Good catch. If some pods sent revoked tokens and the auth service returns 401, but downstream code wraps that into a 503 for client-friendly messages, that fits the symptom. Need logs from the auth service for those req ids.

amy: Found trace for `req_42a1`: auth service returned `401` at 09:13:02, gateway returned `503` to client, with message `upstream_error`. Full snippet:

```
trace_id: t-0a9f
09:13:02 auth-service - validate_token - token=redacted - result=INVALID
09:13:02 gateway - proxy - upstream_error - auth-service returned 401, mapping -> 503
```

sara: So root cause likely: some hosts still presenting old/rotated keys because their sidecar didn't pick up new secret. That matches the 30% failure rate (subset of pods).

lee: We need to confirm which pods still had the old secret. Ryan — can you run `kubectl get pods -l app=acme-worker -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{@.metadata.name}:{@.spec.containers[*].env}'` or check `vault-agent` logs for refresh events?

ryan: Running checks now. Quick findings: most acme-worker pods reported successful secret fetch at 09:10:15, but 7 pods show last fetch at 08:59:50. Those pods are on node `gpu-16-ax`. Vault logs show those agent instances returned a 429 from KMS at 09:09 and then backoff kicked in. The agent reconciler didn't retry aggressively due to the 5m refresh interval.

lee: So KMS throttle + increased sidecar refresh interval = pods kept old creds and got revoked. That would explain immediate failure pattern.

jordan: Customer wants a rollback or fix asap. They've disabled their auto-retry and are getting unhappy.

sara: Immediate mitigation: can we re-issue a temporary allow rule (grace) for the previous key ID so old-presented keys still authenticate for a short window? Or re-run a targeted restart of affected pods?

amy: We can do both. Easiest fastest: restart the 7 affected pods to trigger secret fetch now. I'll run `kubectl rollout restart deployment/acme-worker --field-selector` to target them. But need approval - this touches customer Dedicated infra.

ryan: I'm going to also temporarily loosen our revocation enforcement for that org in auth-service: flip `auth.allow_rotated_key_grace` for org `acme` to `true` for 15 minutes. That will allow the old key to work for a short window while we rectify sidecar behavior. I'll update the flag and monitor.

lee: Please document the change and add a verification step. Also schedule a rollback of that flag automatically after 15 minutes.

ryan: Done. Flag set at 09:25 UTC. Auto-revert job scheduled.

amy: Restarted the 7 pods at 09:28. Logs show successful vault-agent fetch at 09:28:12 with the new key. Verified gateway traces for `req_42a1` now show 200 for subsequent retries.

sara: Customer confirmed major drop in failures from 30% -> 0.5% after restarts. They're very grateful. :thumbsup:

lee: Postmortem actions: 1) revert sidecar refresh interval change (or make it small for rotation windows), 2) add KMS throttle handling to agent so rotations are retried aggressively on fetch failures, 3) add a pre-rotation probe that verifies at least N% of pods successfully fetch the new secret before issuing revoke.

amy: I'll file a PR to add the pre-rotation probing check and a dashboard that shows % of pods with current secret version per org.

ryan: I'll create a vault-agent patch: on `fetch` failures, exponential backoff starting at 5s and cap at 60s, and treat a rotation event as high priority to bypass longer intervals.

jordan: CS note: I'll follow up with AcmeCorp, explain the mitigation and the plan. We'll offer a credit for the outage window.

oncall-bot: INC-2026-780 updated: mitigated. Postmortem required.

lee: Quick action items (assigned): sara - coordinate customer comms; amy - PR for pre-rotation probe; ryan - vault-agent retries + revert config; lee - add rotation runbook update. I'll loop in Security for approval of the temporary grace flow.

sara: Thanks all. Leaving thread open until postmortem doc is up.

vault-agent: INFO: 2026-10-14T09:09:05Z - KMS request throttled (429) - backoff triggered

vault-agent: INFO: 2026-10-14T09:28:12Z - Secret fetch succeeded - version v20261014-3

amy: Filing postmortem draft in #postmortems and will link here when ready.

sara: Closing for now — feel free to add anything else. :wave:
